how: The starter calls for help building a specified logo of blue dots with a white border.
The member who proposes and specifies the logo fits the revised starter role independently of subsequent joining.
The opening proposal supplies the object of the same member's subsequent help call.
Selecting a logo and specifying dots and a border supplies the minimal design-proposal form without collective debate.
A member reports trying to build and the organiser later confirms completion.
A reported building attempt follows the call, supporting the sequence without identifying what caused the member to start.
The changed plan circulates a linked new location for building the logo.
Instructions and a changed plan do not establish a template settling an argued design.
Bare thanks acknowledges the proposed relocation discussion without asking for anything back.
A complaint-bearing placement answer and later thanks to another proposal cannot test the proposed preference mechanism or unwritten answers.
Visitors describe scripts maintaining their flag, establishing neighbouring automation rather than confirmed deployment for the logo.
Under strain, seeking automated assistance is evidenced, but a conclusion of deployed extra placements requires evidence beyond an offer and promised grid preparation.
Instructions and another room's moderator contact cannot test a cross-room frequency claim or exclude decisions outside the supplied record.
A late call and neighbouring script pressure do not establish that members judged their own hands insufficient.
A report of being overrun and a visitor's attempted defence show preservation contested by old scripts.
Reported completion precedes attempted defence against persistent overwriting, supporting the sequence without attributing every changed pixel.
Visitors explain continuing overwrites through flag-maintenance scripts and sleeping users rather than treating every pixel as intentional hostility.
Apply known-form maintenance to neighbouring flag scripts without assuming that logo defenders erase their own agreed changes or that failed notification finally ends the work.
The organiser proposes and sends a truce to the box builders.
The organiser contacts a neighbouring room to ask that expanding flags spare the logo.
Participants propose alternative sites and report a continuing deal to build above a neighbouring wordmark.
The organiser carries messages between rooms and reports a direct reply without evidence of a formal appointment.
Negotiation across a language gap proceeds through asking a French speaker, receiving a reasoned refusal, and substituting machine translation.
Explanations, correction and acknowledgment help participants understand neighbouring flags while pursuing agreement.
The organiser reports an alliance expected to watch the logo, establishing a claimed bilateral tie rather than verified reciprocal protection.
The alliance report does not establish formation because both works faced a shared threat.
The request for neighbours to leave the dots alone explicitly names threatened flag expansion.
Negotiation can begin during building and continue alongside defence rather than following upkeep as a separate completed stage.
A later relocation proposal and ongoing negotiations after an overrun fit preparing a rebuild without establishing completed relocation.
The evidenced endpoint is negotiating where to rebuild, so completed relocation and explicit fight-versus-move deliberation must not be inferred.
The stated practical reason for relocating is persistent flag scripts rather than a judgment of insufficient hands.
The suggested new site receives a promise to stay inside the neighbour's own logo and an apology.
A verbal boundary commitment does not establish realised restraint when old scripts continue overwriting the work.
Realising restraint requires reaching the sleeping users whose old scripts continue changing the protected logo.
A visitor explicitly disclaims speaking for the neighbouring room while discussing whether it will allow the logo to stay.
The disclaimer accompanies a proposed appeal rather than following an established agreement, placing it outside the bounded after-agreement mechanism.
A request for neighbouring bots to help rebuild receives a conditional offer alongside an explanation of limited account capacity.
Strain leads to requesting and conditionally arranging help here, while actual delivery remains unresolved.
The boundary assurance is answered by a rebuild request, showing the negotiation channel being used to seek assistance.
Bot assistance requires usable images, a location, moderator contact, and spare account capacity beyond the helper's own unfinished picture.
The offer develops through agreeing image specifications and preparing a grid before the helper can finish the remaining preparation.
An ongoing relocation deal answers a defence report, making moving preparations and holding the current logo concurrent activities.
Moderator contact for bot assistance and a pending location deal cannot establish a completed host-governed guest arrangement.
Visitors explaining national flags do not establish that the host room adopted a national identity or enacted an inherited political quarrel.
Explanations of neighbouring flags do not establish a prior quarrel carried in by the host room.
Historical explanations without an accompanying host-room attack call cannot test the cross-room claim linking prior ties to attacked rivals.
The logo proposal and precise building instructions do not establish host-subreddit parody or an April Fools takeover.
The placement call does not establish containment of canvas talk or prove that containment was unnecessary.
The call does not establish a canvas-post flood causing the host to impose boundaries.
An arrival celebrates completion and a later visitor praises the discovered logo.
Celebration and confirmation of completion are directly connected in the reply exchange without establishing a permanent end to building.
A brief overrun report records the logo's immediate fate while defence and relocation remain active.
Celebration precedes reporting damage, but the sequence does not establish that celebrating caused record preservation.
The last coded action concerns negotiating a new site and leaves post-event continuation unobserved.
An overrun report and further relocation negotiations do not establish that recording produced a lasting project.
Correcting flag history during active negotiations cannot test disputes over post-placement versions or accounts of the event.
Neighbouring expansion and scripts are described, but the supplied evidence does not establish that the host room called for an attack.
The call is followed by building and a proposed truce without showing recruitment turning into an attack call.
Blaming square builders and reporting an overrun do not establish a continuing verbal contest with a rival.

A visitor reports relocation discussion in an existing neighbouring chat and brings that planning into the thread.
The record shows the neighbour's relayed discussion rather than a completed chat decision or wholesale transfer of the host room's planning.
Visitors explain and correct what the neighbouring flags depict, and the organiser acknowledges learning from the explanation.
A visitor finds the logo around neighbouring canvas art and comes into the room to praise its builders.
The organiser uses the visitor's timely arrival to request cross-language help, which the visitor declines for insufficient French.
Casual laughter and a question about friendly Canadians do not establish a new canvas joke taken up by the room.
An early update changes the building location before the later report of completion.
Changing the building site is evidenced, but whether any loss preceded that early move remains unresolved.
Calling for a logo does not establish that a new community formed around the canvas mark.
Flag-history correction and an expansion apology do not establish policing of slurs or disputes over offensive jokes.
An album-logo proposal and visitor praise do not establish outreach to the represented creators, press, or outside addressees.
Requests to spare the mark and apologies for expansion do not establish an argument over whether covering art is fair.
Reporting an overrun does not show anyone leaving under strain or participants repairing a personal quarrel.
A direct public reply and machine translation do not establish secret planning, infiltration, or concealment from rivals.
A complaint about square builders and an overrun report do not establish attacks on the room's own work prompted by objections to canvas posts.
Sleeping users leave old scripts running, making personal availability a constraint on changing the automated placements.
A report of limited edits per account does not establish site faults, exceptional timer behaviour, or tested fixes.
Finding the logo and explaining neighbouring national flags do not establish dual membership or a response of torn or proud belonging.
